clue.text: Jack gets a thumbs-down from us as a writer

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
something from us is ours, giving the possessive OUR
a thumbs-down is a refusal, a no

explanation.surface: A card player, Jack, is rejected by the group as a would-be author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'as' are only links; 'from us' means belonging to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Journo is informal slang for a journalist, a professional writer for newspapers.

clue.text: Old lover not devoid of affection is one to reach out

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
someone not lacking affection is tender, loving

explanation.surface: A former partner who still feels warmly keeps trying to make contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that extends lengthens or stretches, so it is a thing that reaches further out.

clue.text: Remote part of Scotland has all dads suffering with thinness

indicators.note: the letters are in distress, so they are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: In a far-flung corner of Scotland, every father is wasting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is only a link; the anagram uses ALL DADS and THINNESS together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetland Islands lie far north of mainland Scotland, its most remote archipelago.

clue.text: Military hospital involved in upsetting matter, vehicle accident

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up in the other, so it sits inside
in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: pus is the matter that oozes from a wound
MASH is a mobile army surgical hospital

explanation.surface: A field hospital deals with a disturbing business after a road crash.
explanation.walkthrough: MASH is the famous American army field hospital of the TV series; 'upsetting' suits a down clue, reading from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-up is a violent collision, typically a car crash.

clue.text: Where Africans were once trained to fear teenagers

indicators.note: the letters are drilled into a new formation, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has been taught to be scared of adolescents.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Free State was a historic Boer republic, later a South African province, now gone.

clue.text: Scottish king finally boarded a French vessel

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word boarded

parts.note: un is French for a
a can is a container, a vessel

explanation.surface: A Scottish monarch eventually climbs aboard a French ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan was a medieval king of Scots, murdered by Macbeth in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: The first boy maybe to be heard in song

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so its sound gives a different spelling

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A firstborn son might be featured in a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: A firstborn son is traditionally the one who inherits, the successor to the estate.

clue.text: Cable's attempt to influence

definitions.meaning: coaxial cable, as used for television aerials
to persuade gently, to cajole or wheedle

explanation.definitionFit: Coax is short for coaxial cable, and also a verb for gently persuading someone.

clue.text: Poor person acting as king let off

indicators.note: taking a word off means removing it from the longer one

parts.note: Hamlet was a prince, but the play's ghost is King Hamlet, his father

explanation.surface: A bad actor plays a monarch and is excused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes LET from HAMLET; the surface reads 'let off' as being excused.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a performer who overacts badly, a poor thespian.

clue.text: Sent packing, using the fourth itinerary

parts.note: an itinerary is a planned route
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is dispatched along the fourth planned journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an enemy is to drive it away in defeat, to send it packing.

clue.text: Stop to have a break, having crossed river

indicators.note: the break spans the river, so it goes either side of it

parts.note: a break is a rest, so this gives A plus REST

explanation.surface: Pause for a breather after getting over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest is to halt or bring something to a standstill.

clue.text: Undemanding job could be nice, sure!

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: An easy post — that would be pleasant, certainly!
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position requiring little or no work.

clue.text: Helpful disposition diverted to dangerous ends

indicators.note: the letters are sent off course, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind nature turned towards wicked purposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindliness and an obliging temperament make up a friendly, helpful character.

clue.text: Book with some English explorer

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run hidden inside them

explanation.surface: A volume comes with an English adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is H. Rider Haggard's adventure novel, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the title of a famous Victorian novel by H. Rider Haggard.

clue.text: I had to be immersed in plant life of place, US location

indicators.note: the piece is plunged into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: flora is the plant life of a region
I'd is short for I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being surrounded by a region's vegetation in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is a state in the south-east of the United States.

clue.text: Record number in maths class?

definitions.meaning: a written record of events, such as a ship's journal
a logarithm, a number studied in maths lessons

explanation.definitionFit: A log is a journal of events, and also short for logarithm, an exponent used in maths.

clue.text: Bishop more foolhardy and more arrogant

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rasher is the comparative of rash, reckless

explanation.surface: A churchman who is more reckless and more conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means cocky and self-assertive, so its comparative means cockier.

clue.text: More than one fighter joins to capture island

indicators.note: the outer word seizes the other and holds it inside

parts.note: solders means joins metal with molten alloy

explanation.surface: A unit links up in order to seize an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are fighting men and women of an army, plural fighters.

clue.text: The tale about the hare that lost, say

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, rearranged

explanation.surface: A fable concerns the overconfident hare beaten by the tortoise.
explanation.walkthrough: In Aesop's fable the speedy hare loses a race to the tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: The hare is a fast runner, an example of a sporty competitor in a race.

clue.text: Like ghost, can act mysteriously, in a desperate hurry?

indicators.note: the letters behave in a strange way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Like a spirit, someone can behave in an eerie manner when rushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing against the clock means working rapidly to meet a deadline, hence frantic haste.

clue.text: Like all the pretty maids, fighting

definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme Mary, Mary has pretty maids all lined up

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme ends 'And pretty maids all in a row'; a row is also a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lined up one after another, and also engaged in a noisy quarrel.

clue.text: Mark unknown sort of territory

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An unidentified sign on a map indicates a type of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a territory governed by a distant country.

clue.text: You're welcome? Never!

definitions.meaning: a polite reply to thanks, meaning it was no trouble
an emphatic denial, in no way whatever

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a gracious reply to thanks and an emphatic no.

clue.text: Due to get nothing before middle of the week

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing
Wednesday, abbreviated Wed, is midweek

explanation.surface: Someone is set to receive nothing ahead of Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is owed is payable, outstanding.

clue.text: Possible component of meal that doesn't matter

definitions.meaning: a custard, cream and sponge dessert served as a pudding
a thing of little importance, a trivial matter

explanation.definitionFit: A layered pudding course and a thing of no importance share the same word.

clue.text: Mo awarded the silver medal?

definitions.meaning: mo is slang for a moment, a very short time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mo' looks like Mo Farah, the British gold medallist, but it is short for moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief moment is a tick of time, and the runner-up in a race comes after the winner.

clue.text: I disapprove of that teacher putting 18 off

indicators.note: taking the piece off removes it from the word

parts.note: a tutor is a private teacher
the answer to 18 is fighters, and OR, other ranks, are soldiers below officer rank

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about a teacher who puts troops off.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is SOLDIERS; OR (other ranks) means ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut is an exclamation of mild disapproval or impatience.

clue.text: Band's sound

definitions.meaning: a circular band, as on a finger
to chime, as a bell does

explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a circle of metal worn as jewellery, and also the chiming of a bell.
